mainEntity.name: How do I know if my house structure and foundation can handle a second‑story addition?

acceptedAnswer.text:
You can’t safely assume your existing structure can support a second story; you need a structural assessment. A licensed engineer or experienced design‑build team evaluates foundation size, soil conditions, framing, and lateral bracing.

Overloading an undersized foundation can cause cracking, settlement, and serious safety issues. Sometimes strengthening or partial rebuilding is required before going up.

Key factors:
- Current foundation size, depth, and condition
- Existing wall and roof framing and load paths
- Local seismic requirements and lateral bracing needs
- Cost difference between reinforcing vs. choosing a ground‑level addition

Before committing to a second story concept, budget for an engineering review. If the required upgrades are extensive, compare the cost and disruption to an alternative ground‑floor extension or reconfiguration of your existing layout.
